references.text: The Israelites gave up their gold rings, which were used to make the golden calf. This shows how gold jewelry could be used for idol worship.
War spoils of gold from the Midianites were given as an offering to the Lord, including bracelets, rings, and other ornaments.
Description of women's jewelry and adornments, including crescents and earrings, reflecting the jewelry culture of that time.
Earlier in the same chapter, the crescent-shaped ornaments on the camels' necks taken as war spoils by Gideon's men are mentioned.
Gideon used the gold to make an ephod that became a snare for Israel, showing the consequences of the gold spoils.
Nose rings and gold bracelets given as gifts, illustrating the value of gold jewelry in that culture.
Ishmaelite merchants with camels traveling from Gilead, showing trade routes and camel use in the region.
